roles.purpose: Dimension that reinforces, qualifies or creates tension with the anchor.
Meaningful dimension that expands the snapshot into another behavioural family.

anchor: Choose the highest distinctiveness dimension with valid data.
Use response consistency as a future tie-breaker when available.
counterbalance: Prefer a dimension with a curated relationship to the anchor.
Prefer a different family unless a same-family relationship is materially more informative.
Do not replace a candidate more than 12 distinctiveness points stronger solely to gain diversity.
breadth: Prefer a family not yet represented.
Require meaningful distinctiveness before using social_transparency solely for diversity.
Use the next strongest valid candidate when no cross-family candidate is meaningful.
cluster_exception: When the top three dimensions are in one family and the strongest outside-family candidate trails the third by more than 12 distinctiveness points, retain the clustered top three.
Use the clustered relationship module to explain that concentration rather than forcing diversity.
diversity_tolerance: An outside-family candidate may replace the third-ranked same-family candidate only when it is no more than 12 distinctiveness points weaker.
The replacement must add a materially different behavioural lens.

overlap.section1: Soft penalty for direct repetition of the winning recognition claim.
overlap.section2: Soft penalty when the dimension interpretation would repeat the same specific behaviour as a selected card.
overlap.principle: Never suppress a genuinely defining dimension merely to create artificial novelty.

display.percentile: Retain overall percentile and lower-centre-higher visual scale.
display.benchmark_copy: Benchmark position may appear in the visual area. Interpretation and summary must remain behavioural.
display.summary: Assemble from one anchor module, one relationship module and one direction-aware breadth module.
display.transition: Render separately from the dynamic summary.
display.breadth_definition: Breadth explains what the third selected dimension adds. High/low interaction between the first two dimensions belongs in the relationship module.

relationship_types.reinforcing: Two dimensions strengthen the same behavioural story.
relationship_types.contrasting: One behaviour is expressed more prominently than another.
relationship_types.counterbalancing: One dimension qualifies the implication of another.
relationship_types.tension: The dimensions pull toward competing forms of involvement or control.
relationship_types.context_dependent: Central or mixed results suggest variation by task or situation.
relationship_types.clustered: All three selected dimensions concentrate in one behavioural family.
relationship_types.broadly_integrated: The three dimensions span several behavioural families.

synthetic_tests.reason: The strongest outside-family distinctiveness is 5, which trails the third thinking dimension by 33 points. Diversity must not override the defining cluster.
